scope: Clear stale published active skin identity after a memory-bound session has restored visuals and is waiting for deferred resource retirement
rootCause: SkinApplyStatus.AwaitingTargets represented both an unavailable-target wait that retained valid old visuals and a restore-complete retirement wait with no active visuals. SkinRuntimeSession knew which state existed, but SkinApplyResult did not transport that fact, so SkinLibraryRuntimeController retained and published its old activeId and activeTree.

remediation.contract: SkinApplyResult.PreviousVisualsRestored explicitly marks restore-complete waits. SkinRuntimeSession sets it on the memory-pressure restore result and every subsequent retirement-barrier result while CurrentPack is null, and preserves it through retirement diagnostics. SkinLibraryRuntimeController clears activeId, activeTree and activeMode immediately when that flag is observed while retaining the pending candidate and direct retry state.
retainedBehavior: AwaitingTargets with genuinely retained old character visuals keeps the old active identity
OFF successful restoration publishes no active identity
ON-to-ROTATE memory pressure publishes vanilla/no active pack until retirement completes
RestoreFailed retains the old active identity because rollback can leave it genuinely active
Delayed retirement performs no successor allocation and retries the frozen candidate

deviceDeferrals: Android bundle identity and managed parity
Unity renderer, GPU and shader appearance
physical-device resource pressure and death/respawn behavior
evidenceBoundary: The integrated controller/session test proves observation identity, delayed-release accounting, retry and successor publication on host fakes. Exact managed compiles and rewrite verification prove source and binary compatibility, not Android runtime acceptance.
